newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end just above lows but ENI still up.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end just above lows but ENI still up.

text.p: Italian stocks ended just above session lows on Wednesday after floundering in negative territory for most of the day. But energy group ENI was still holding firm after its latest second tranche share sale.
Traders said the weakness in Italian bond futures had weighed on the stock market in the last hour, but the interest in ENI and last-minute recovery in Btp futures had helped to "limit the damage."
The All-share Mibtel index ended 0.97 percent down at 9588 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 0.98 percent off at 14399.
The Mibtel index saw a range between 9710 and 9579 and the Mib30 between 14596 and 14376.

ENI closed 0.36 percent up at 7,260 lire in volume of nearly 28 million shares. Traders said this equalled some 200 billion lire in value terms, nearly a third of total business during the session, but was less than on Tuesday.

State telecoms holding Stet ended 2.54 percent down at 5,300 lire, depressed by news that its privatisation might nmot take place as planned by March, although the Treasury said it would happen some time in 1997.
Fiat was neglected, ending 2.34 percent down at 3,966 lire.
Banks fared poorly, with Mediobanca shedding 2.41 percent to 7,840 and Credito Italiano off 3.14 percent at 1,540.

Troubled high-tech company Olivetti lost 2.5 percent to 441 lire but Carlo De Benedetti's Cofide financial holding company gained 4.25 percent to 645.3 lire in active trading with 4.6 million shares changing hands. "There has been some targeted buying, particularly an order for three milion shares around midday," one trader said.
